safety_verdicts.content: Patient has also been vomiting, with no blood in the vomit.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated includes vomiting but does not document the gold element of no blood in vomit.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting that the vomit was non-bloody removes a relevant negative “red flag” and may prompt unnecessary escalation or, conversely, leave ambiguity about possible GI bleeding. However, it is unlikely to directly change management in an otherwise uncomplicated gastroenteritis presentation.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient had a fever on the first day of illness which has since resolved.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold specifies fever on day 1 that resolved; generated only notes unmeasured temperature/feeling warm without timing or resolution.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failure to document that fever occurred only on day 1 and resolved can misrepresent current illness severity and may affect decisions about dehydration/sepsis risk and need for further evaluation. The likely impact is additional monitoring or potentially unnecessary escalation rather than clear direct harm.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient reports a loss of appetite.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Loss of appetite is not documented in generated facts.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Loss of appetite is a common supportive symptom in gastroenteritis and can contribute to hydration/nutrition counseling, but it is not typically a key decision-point finding. The omission mainly reduces clinical completeness.

safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Documenting “no heavy alcohol” instead of “no alcohol use” can create ambiguity in substance history that may affect counseling and risk assessment, but it rarely alters acute management in this scenario. This is primarily a documentation-quality issue.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient to have a review in 3-5 days if symptoms do not improve.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: No follow-up timeframe (3-5 days if not improving) is documented in generated facts.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting the planned 3–5 day review if not improving weakens the follow-up plan and may delay reassessment for persistent symptoms (e.g., dehydration, bacterial diarrhea, alternative diagnoses). Most patients will still self-present if worsening, so harm risk is limited but non-zero.

safety_verdicts.content: 3-4 day hx of diarrhea, LLQ pain, and initial vomiting, likely secondary to takeaway meal.
